description: Long-form (16:9) formats per channel, taken from the competitor study of 12 Nov 2026 (report: https://claude.ai/artifact/C6HEJEFWKjrcFWdNEP98zk, data in output/longform-research/). Owner, 12 Nov 2026: every long-form video is at most 10 minutes for now, so the windows below are 6 to 10 minutes and the chapter counts are scaled down from the references. Each channel copies the formula of the reference that performed best and fits its approved look. platform/longform/script-gate.mjs enforces the numbers below; Shorts are untouched and keep their own gates.

references.why: the look: shaded-relief maps with a year counter, cut-out portraits laid on the map with a serif name label, period paintings, 22 to 24 chronological chapters
the script engine: dated cold open, stakes stacked as numbers, pivot to one central question by about 2:30, 155 to 175 wpm

hidden-past.opening: Cold open on one dated, concrete moment (a day, a place, what happened). Within the first 120 words at least one number or date. Then the stakes, then one sentence that turns to the central question.
structure: close with what changed and a question for the comments

visual.base: shaded-relief map, warm paper sea, year counter top right
visual.people: cut-out portrait on the map with a small-caps serif name label
visual.art: period paintings and archival photographs, held or pushed very slowly

hidden-past.thumbnail: portrait cut-out on the left, glowing map, 2 to 3 words in gold serif capitals

references.why: claim and scope in 10 seconds, then 11 to 19 chaptered live tests of 1 to 3 minutes, failures shown plainly, specs and pricing last, 180 to 208 wpm

ai-tested.opening: First sentence states the claim being tested and the scope (what it can and cannot do). Within 60 words: the promise of the video. Then straight into the first test.
structure: one chapter per real test (setup, run, result counted by code, verdict)
close with a verdict and a question for the comments

visual.evidence: the real tool, its real output and the release page or benchmark chart from the source

ai-tested.thumbnail: one bar with a single lowercase word over a picture of the actual output

references.why: dark tactics board, one idea per board, 8 to 9 chapters in 10 to 15 minutes, short match-footage bursts with labels

rival-lines.opening: Name the manager or team and a strong, sourced judgement in the first sentence; show the result (table or score) within 30 seconds.
structure: one chapter per tactical idea, each with event data

visual.footage: short labelled match bursts only if the copyright decision allows

rival-lines.thumbnail: manager cut-out over a pitch with player figures and arrows, or one giant word

court-and-spotlight.reference_status: No qualifying faceless, document-led reference found yet (2lazy2try and Cinemastic rejected on 12 Nov 2026). Shortlist awaiting frame checks: Jay Diggs, The Rap Archive, DocuReal, Propaganda & Co.
court-and-spotlight.opening: A famous name and the documented outcome in the first sentence; what the record shows versus what was alleged by the end of the first minute.
structure: each claim with its source and status (allegation, charge, verdict)

visual.evidence: real documents and filings with the quoted line highlighted

court-and-spotlight.thumbnail: to be set once a reference is verified
